output:
I didn't run the install. This directory is not an n8n checkout, and there is nothing here for npm to install into.

What I found:

- **The repo is context-report**, cloned from github.com/open-coder-ai/context-report. The worktree lives at /home/user/cr-w17.
- **The working directory is a measurements folder.** It holds an evals directory, an out directory, run.json, and two log files. There is no package.json and no lockfile of any kind.
- **A missing node_modules is expected here**, since nothing declares dependencies. Running npm install in this folder would only drop a stray, empty package-lock.json into the repo.

The one broader search I tried, looking for a package.json or an n8n checkout elsewhere under /home/user, was blocked by permissions, so I could not confirm whether an n8n clone exists on this machine at all.

If you point me at the actual n8n directory, I can run the install there. Note that n8n itself is a pnpm monorepo, so the right command in that checkout is `pnpm install` rather than `npm install`, which would fail on its workspace layout.
